name: South Africa
headline: South Africa: +1.1% growth in 2025, 3.2% inflation, debt 78% of GDP
sections: South Africa is a $427 billion economy (2025), the world's 40th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.1% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $16K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 6.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 32.4% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 59.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 78% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 69% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.6% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −0.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 61% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −0.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 80% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 66.3 years (2024). Population: 63.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
